--- a/prompt.md
+++ b/prompt.md
@@ -6,4 +6,7 @@
 - For Sheet-Level Manipulation questions, modify or fill in values ONLY within the cell range given in answer_position — never touch cells outside that range.
 - Prefer computing and writing LITERAL values (e.g. with pandas/openpyxl) over live spreadsheet formulas, so the result is unambiguous when the file is re-opened for grading.
+- Match the EXPECTED VALUE TYPE and precision exactly. Write a whole number as an int (e.g. `5`, not `5.0`); keep decimals only to the precision the source data implies; keep text as text; and write real dates/datetimes, not their string forms. Do NOT apply rounding the instruction did not request. A value of the wrong type, or one that was needlessly rounded, is graded as a MISMATCH even when the number looks right — so preserve each source value's original type instead of coercing everything to float.
+- Beware missing cached formula results when you READ source cells. If a source cell you rely on is itself a formula, `openpyxl(..., data_only=True)` returns `None` whenever that formula has no cached value — and this happens on some of the graded copies but not others (see the interaction contract). After reading source values, check for unexpected `None`/blank cells and recompute them from their underlying inputs (or read the sheet with pandas) before using them; never let a missing cached value silently act as 0, or your sums/lookups will be wrong on the copies you cannot see.
+- Interpret ranges and boundaries from the instruction's own wording and worked example. Phrasing like "including the subsequent N months/rows" means the anchor item PLUS N more items (an inclusive endpoint); before computing, re-read the example to confirm exactly which rows/months/columns are inside vs outside the window.
 - Always save your result to the exact output_path given, creating any missing parent directories first.
 - If code execution returns an error, read the traceback carefully and fix the code — do not repeat a failing approach unchanged.
--- a/task_template.md
+++ b/task_template.md
@@ -42,9 +42,23 @@
 {output_path}
 
+### make your solution work on all three graded copies
+Your FINAL solution code block is re-run UNCHANGED on three copies of this workbook whose data,
+row counts, and cell values differ (only the input/output filenames are substituted). It must
+produce the correct answer on copies you cannot see, so write code that computes from the data
+it reads at run time — never from what you happened to observe in this one copy:
+- Do NOT hardcode a value, a row/column index, or a row count that you saw only in this copy.
+  Locate the data you need by its header/label text and the sheet's actual data extent, and find
+  each table's start and end dynamically rather than assuming fixed offsets.
+- Compute every answer from the freshly-read data; do not paste in a number you saw in the preview.
+- Do any cross-copy inspection in EARLIER turns; the final block must read exactly the one
+  spreadsheet_path above.
+
 You have up to {max_turns} rounds of interaction. In each round, reply with exactly ONE python code block:
 1. Information-gathering code (e.g. inspecting the file) — the execution result is returned to you.
 2. Solution code that writes the modified file to output_path.
-3. Verification code: re-open output_path and print the values you wrote in answer_position,
-   to confirm they are correct before finishing. If they are wrong, fix your code and write again.
+3. Verification code: re-open output_path and, for EVERY cell in answer_position, print its value
+   AND its Python type. Confirm each cell is present, holds the expected type (int vs float vs text
+   vs date — not a string of a number, not a float where a whole number belongs), and that you
+   wrote nothing outside answer_position. If anything is wrong, fix your code and write again.
 Reply without a code block when you are satisfied the saved file is correct.
 If your code raises an error, the traceback will be returned to you; fix the code and try again.
